cards.text: It's the days of King Josiah, king of Judah, and the LORD speaks to Jeremiah, His prophet. He asks, "Have you seen what faithless Israel has done?" Then He answers His own question: "She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree to prostitute herself there."

cards.question: Israel has been chasing other gods on every high hill. After all that, what did God think she would do?

cards.text: But she did not return. And her unfaithful sister Judah saw the whole thing from the front row.

cards.question: Because faithless Israel committed adultery, what did God give her before sending her away?
Judah watched Israel get sent away, and it scared Judah into staying faithful.

cards.text: Judah had no fear and did the same thing, while Israel committed adultery with stones and trees. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer with dead batteries for years, and not ONCE did I ask one for a blessing.

cards.question: In spite of all this, how did Judah come back to God?

cards.text: Pretense. Judah showed up the way some of us show up to a work meeting: camera off, mic muted, already back in bed.

cards.question: The LORD tells Jeremiah that faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than unfaithful Judah.

cards.text: WAIT. The one who got sent away with divorce papers comes out looking BETTER? Then God sends Jeremiah to call toward the north, and the message starts with "Return, O faithless Israel," and keeps going.

cards.question: God says He will no longer look on Israel with anger, because He is ___.
God says His anger won't last forever. What's the one thing He asks Israel to do?

cards.text: That's it, friend: no forms in triplicate, no waiting room, just own what you did. Then God calls again, "Return, O faithless children," and says He is their master.

cards.question: God says He'll take them, one from a city and two from a family, and bring them to ___.
God promises to give them shepherds after His own heart. What will those shepherds feed them with?

cards.text: Then God looks ahead to "those days," when they multiply and increase in the land. And He brings up the ark of the covenant.

cards.question: In those days, what does God say about the ark of the covenant?

answers.text: No one will remember or miss it
A greater one will be built
It will be carried to the nations

cards.question: At that time, what will they call Jerusalem?
At that time, all the nations will be gathered in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD.
In those days, the house of Judah will walk with the house of ___, coming together from the land of the north.

cards.text: Then God says what He longed for: "How I long to make you My sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations!"

cards.question: God says He thought they would call Him ___ and never turn away from following Him.

cards.text: But that's not how it went. "But as a woman may betray her husband, so you have betrayed Me, O house of Israel," declares the LORD.
Then a voice is heard on the barren heights. It's the children of Israel, weeping and begging for mercy.

cards.question: Why are the children of Israel weeping and begging for mercy on the barren heights?

answers.text: They had turned away and forgotten the LORD
Enemies had taken away all their land
Their king had been killed in battle

cards.question: Then God calls out, "Return, O faithless children." What does He promise to do about their faithlessness?

cards.text: And THIS time, they answer: "Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God." Friend, that's the sound of somebody finally picking up after the phone rang all day.

cards.question: The people say their salvation comes from the hills and the mountains.

cards.text: Then they admit what that shameful god has cost them. From their youth, it has consumed what their fathers worked for: flocks, herds, even their sons and daughters.

cards.question: With all that out in the open, what do the people say they'll do with their shame?
The people confess that from their youth even to this day, they have not obeyed the voice of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks, and it starts with an if: "If you will return, O Israel, return to Me," declares the LORD.

cards.question: If Israel will return, what does God say they need to remove from His sight?
If they swear by the LORD in truth, in justice and in righteousness, then the ___ will be blessed by Him.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells the men of Judah and Jerusalem, "Break up your unplowed ground, and do not sow among the thorns." It's like dough that sat out all night: NOTHING gets stamped into it until you work it first.

cards.question: God tells the men of Judah to circumcise themselves to the LORD. What does He tell them to remove the foreskins of?
God warns Judah that if they don't change, His wrath will flare up for a moment and then pass.

cards.text: A fire no one can put out, because of their evil deeds. Heavy words to end on, friend, but listen to the one word this passage keeps calling out: return.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Return, O faithless children.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Israel and Judah first appear (cards 1 and 3) without saying who they are. The baker isn't told that Israel is the northern kingdom, already sent away, and Judah is the southern kingdom Josiah rules. Without that, the two sisters, the certificate of divorce and the call 'toward the north' (3:12, 3:18) are hard to follow.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card says Josiah is king of Judah and Jeremiah is the LORD's prophet. Both facts come from outside the passage (Jeremiah 1:1-2). The card cites only Jeremiah 3:6, and the output format has a single verses field for the card.
findings.question: When a story card uses a helpful fact from outside the passage, where does its reference go? Should it be added to the card's verses field, written in the card text, or left out?

findings.problem: 'Judah had no fear and did the same thing, while Israel committed adultery with stones and trees' links the two with 'while', a timing connection the text doesn't make. Verse 3:9 is background on what Israel had done ('Israel had defiled the land').

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 3:17 also promises 'They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.' This heart change sets up the call to circumcise their hearts in 4:4, but no card tells it. The walkthrough skips from the nations gathering straight to verse 3:18.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 7 of the stop's 13 choice cards. True or false and fill in the blank have only 3 each, so one type dominates the stop.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact picture in the people's words: 'Let us lie down in our shame.' Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason to 'Lie down in it' over 'Wash it away'. This is like the Psalm 23 example of guessing what David's head is anointed with.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
